questions.q: Describe the three layers of the Earth's interior.
answer: The Earth is made up of three concentric layers.

answer.text: The outermost and thinnest layer, on which we live. It is about 35 km thick under the continents but only about 5 km under the oceans. Continental crust is mainly silica and alumina (SIAL), and oceanic crust mainly silica and magnesium (SIMA).
The middle layer, lying just beneath the crust and extending to a depth of about 2900 km.
The innermost and hottest layer, made mainly of nickel and iron (NIFE). Its outer part is liquid and its inner part solid.

answer: Together these layers make up the structure of our planet.

questions.q: Describe the three types of rocks and how one changes into another.
answer: Rocks are natural masses of minerals, and they are of three kinds.

answer.text: Formed when molten magma or lava cools and hardens, such as basalt and granite. They are called primary rocks.
Formed when sediments are pressed together in layers over long periods, such as sandstone; they often contain fossils.
Formed when igneous or sedimentary rocks are changed by great heat and pressure — clay becomes slate, limestone becomes marble.
These rocks keep changing into one another over long ages: rocks weather into sediments, sediments harden, heat and pressure transform them, and deep heat can melt rock back into magma.
